finding.claim: MEDIUM (blind, stored SSRF): a user-supplied callbackUrl is stored with no validation and POSTed to by the periodic notifyAll job. An attacker can register http://169.254.169.254/..., http://localhost:PORT/... or other RFC-1918 targets. The scheduler then sends the payload to them every minute. The response is discarded, so this is blind SSRF (internal POSTs, port scanning, timing inference). Fix: parse the URL, require https, check .hostname against a strict allowlist, and block loopback, link-local and RFC-1918 resolved IPs. Re-validate at fetch time.
finding.source: POST /subscribe body field `callbackUrl` (the `callbackUrl` parameter of Jobs.subscribe, Jobs.java:13)
finding.sink: client.send(req, ...) with HttpRequest built from URI.create(cb) (Jobs.java:20-24)

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-controlled URL from the POST /subscribe body
subscriptions.put(name, callbackUrl) stores it with no scheme, host or IP validation (Check 4 stored URL)
notifyAll (runs every minute) iterates subscriptions.values() into cb
URI.create(cb) uses the stored URL directly as the request target
client.send(...) dispatches the POST; the response body is ignored

finding.guards_checked: No validation in subscribe or notifyAll: no scheme check, no host allowlist, no IP blocklist, no re-validation at fetch time. No auth check is visible in this file (the HTTP layer is not in the repo). HttpClient.newHttpClient() uses Redirect.NEVER by default, so redirects are not followed, which does not close the finding. The response is not returned to the caller, so severity is MEDIUM rather than HIGH.

verdict.reason: Jobs.java:13-14 stores the callbackUrl from POST /subscribe unvalidated, and Jobs.java:19-24 passes it to URI.create and client.send with no scheme, host or IP check. The only regex guard in the file is on thumb() at line 30 and doesn't apply here. The HTTP layer isn't in the repo, so I couldn't check whether /subscribe requires authentication.
